text:
incident-bot: PAGE FIRED: svc/embedder-prod (eu-west-1) — 500/502 spike + high latency. Severity: P1. Auto-escalate in 30s if unacknowledged.

lena: Acked, oncall here — looking now.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by lena. Incident timer stopped.

carlos: i'm taking the bridge. quick clarifying q: only eu-west embedder-prod, right? dedicated pools unaffected?

lena: correct — only embedder-prod in eu-west1. Dedicated pools and US regions look fine. Metrics: 502s up ~18% in last 5m, p95 latency ~820ms.

tim: spinning up a staging repro to validate. tagging @maria to shadow in case i need handoff.

maria: shadowing, running live traces now. pulling logs: `kubectl logs -n inference deploy/embedder-prod --since=10m --tail=200`

carlos: logs show repeated upstream timeout: 
```
ERROR embedder: upstream model-server: connection reset by peer
WARN embedder: failed request, retrying (attempt 1)
```

carlos: initial hypothesis: intermittent network drops between embedder and model-server (eu-west rack). i'll attempt a rolling canary restart of two pods.

lena: heads up: PagerDuty escalation window extended to allow mitigation.

carlos: running canary restart on embedder-prod-5 and -6 in eu-west1-canary: 
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/embedder-prod -n inference --selector=zone=eu-west1,canary=true
```

incident-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty will not escalate while alert is acknowledged, but monitor escalation timer if ack removed.

tim: after canary restart: 502s dropped immediately to baseline, p95 down to ~140ms. still seeing a handful of connection resets on pod-3.

maria: running `ss -tanp` on model-server nodes; seeing transient RSTs from node nic 10.10.5.12 to embedder IPs around same timestamps.

lena: customer impact check: ~7.8% of embedding requests in eu-west saw timeouts or 5xx in last 10m. No broad downstream outages reported yet but degraded for some customers. Preparing a short customer note for CS. :warning:

carlos: i'm going to cordon node 10.10.5.12 and migrate pods off for NIC investigation. brief handoff: i need to step out in 12m — @maria please take owner after I reassign on PD.

maria: acknowledged, i'll take ownership. will follow these next steps: 1) confirm node cordon + drain succeeded; 2) check provider NIC metrics; 3) keep PD status updated; 4) create post-incident ticket for NIC flapping.

carlos: cordon & drain started: `kubectl drain node/ip-10-10-5-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — migration in progress.

maria: drain succeeded, pods rescheduled to healthy nodes. monitoring metrics. latency back to normal for >3m.

tim: verified a spike correlating to provider BGP flaps at 03:12:xx — transient but impacted a subset of nodes.

lena: timeline + customer impact summary ready: will post to #customers-incident-updates and link to PD incident.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Ownership transferred to maria. Updated incident status: acknowledged -> ongoing (owner: maria).

maria: taking over. I'll keep watch for 30m, escalate to infra eng if provider NIC errors continue. Creating follow-up ticket INF-4321 with notes and logs.

lena: thanks team — great quick response. handoff complete. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: RESOLUTION NOTE: No more elevated error rates for 10m; monitoring window active. If errors recur, PD will re-open and re-escalate.

maria: final: leaving monitoring alerts on for 1hr, will add remediation items to INF-4321 (node-level NIC monitoring + provider liaison). closing thread in 45m unless new activity.
